items.synopsis: Sending GARP reply packet on a VTEP interface causes flooding in network on QFX5130 and QFX5700 platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved QFX5130 and QFX5700 platforms, Gratuitous Address Resolution Protocol (GARP) flooding occurs in the network when it receives a GARP reply packet on a Virtual Tunnel End Point (VTEP) interface.

items.synopsis: The xmlproxyd process crash is observed in telemetry scenario
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when telemetry services are enabled and the interleaving of telemetry streaming of more than one xmlproxyd sensors can lead to xmlproxyd process crash.

items.synopsis: Delete notifications for sub-interfaces missed in gRPC telemetry
items.description: On Junos platforms, delete notifications for deleted interfaces are not reported through gRPC(Remote Procedure Call) in Telemetry. There is no service impact however notifications on deleted interface are not received.

items.category: MX YT-ZF Linecards Interface Software Category
items.synopsis: Delay in an interface on LC9600 to come up due to repeated flaps
items.description: There is a delay in an interface on LC9600 to come up sometimes due to SerDes re-initing triggered by repeating flaps. Each plane is made of one or several Fabric ASICs (Application-Specific Integrated Circuits). The Fabric ASIC is connected to all the PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) with dedicated links called SerDes. The issue caused a delay in turning up the link from 30 seconds to 80 seconds depending on if the link partner undergoes the same delay. Traffic will not pass on the port until the link is up again.

items.synopsis: EVO: 400GZR: Not able to tune 400G ZR optics to 1554.54nm
items.description: Can't set wavelength 1554.54 nm for 400G ZR and ZR-M optics

items.synopsis: Multiple flaps of the interface will cause the BFD session to be down
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, the IPv4 static route BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) session may stay down if the corresponding interface flaps multiple times.

items.synopsis: The BGP neighbor receives the parent authentication regardless of the authentication setup under the neighbor
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when a BGP neighbor authentication algorithm is configured differently from its parent group. the authentication set up in the parent group is applied to the neighbor instead of using the neighbor's specific algorithm. This causes an authentication error with the neighbor and prevents the connection from being established.

items.synopsis: Few applications fail to start after image upgrade on PTX10003 platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX10003, when 'set chassis fpc pfe power (off|on)' is configured and an image upgrade is performed, certain applications like rpd-sa-agent, rptmd, dot1xd, etc might fail to start post upgrade is completed. Related features and functionalities associated with these applications will not work.

items.category: EVO L3 routing for BCM XGS Platforms
items.synopsis: Unequal traffic distribution on the fabric links
items.description: On QFX5130/QFX5700 Junos OS Evolved platforms functioning as Edge Routed Bridging (ERB) leaf, in EVPN-VXLAN (Ethernet VPN-Virtual Extensible LAN) scenario, the traffic distribution from the leaf device to the spine device over the core links will be unequal.

items.category: EVO VXLAN PFE for BCM XGS Platforms
items.synopsis: LAG doesn't load balance as expected when it is configured as a VXLAN gateway
items.description: On QFX5130/QFX5700 Junos OS Evolved platforms, in Ethernet VPN-Virtual Extensible LAN (EVPN-VXLAN) scenario, traffic is not load balanced on one of the egress member links after VXLAN tunnel termination over the LAG (Link Aggregation Group)/ECMP (Equal Cost Multipath).

items.category: EVO VXLAN PFE for BCM XGS Platforms
items.synopsis: The ECMP routing table does not get updated when underlay L3 interface link flaps in EVPN-VXLAN scenario
items.description: On all Junos Evolved QFX5130/QFX5700 switches, in an EVPN-VXLAN (Ethernet Virtual Private LAN - Virtual Extensible LAN) deployment, Type-2 Overlay ECMP (Equal Cost Multi Path) routing does not happen when the underlay Layer 3 interface is flapped.

items.synopsis: Unstable interface statistic (ingress) going up and down
items.description: The PPS reported for the interface may fluctuate for a few seconds and show either higher or lower value. The chance of this happening is very rare

items.synopsis: The route leaking does not work between different routing instances by using rib-groups on all Junos OS Evolved platforms
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, if the rib-groups is used to import/export routes into the default routing instance from another routing instance, then connectivity fails between those routing instances.

items.synopsis: Commit error will not be seen after deactivating routing-instance applied under firewall filter
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms with enabled firewall filter, deactivating routing-instance which is already applied under the firewall filter, will not show any commit error after commit is issued. This can be seen occasionally and might impact control plane traffic.

items.synopsis: On PTX10001-36MR the VXLAN tunnel termination functionality impacted with global configuration not enabled
items.description: On Junos Evolved PTX10001-36MR platform, the VXLAN (Virtual Extensible LAN) tunnel termination functionality will be impacted when configuration is not enabled for tunnel termination. As the tunnel will not get terminated this will impact the packet forwarding process.

items.synopsis: A high CPU consumption of mcsnoopd process is seen under IGMP-snooping configured scenario leading to its crash
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms with IGMP-snooping (Internet Group Management Protocol) enabled under instance type EVPN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network) with vlan-id=none or unspecified vlan-id there will be a spike in the mcsnoopd process CPU utilization. This will lead to the mcsnoopd process crash and there will be disruptions in the traffic.

items.synopsis: L2ALD core at l2ald_vxlan_ifl_create_msg_build
items.description: During network churn(or during provision- when RVTEP are being discovered/created, network events), it is possible to l2ald cores @ l2ald_vxlan_ifl_create_msg_build.

items.synopsis: The rpd core is seen in the long-running devices with EVPN enabled
items.description: On Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) community object reference count is not handled properly during the process of remote BGP peer routes update event. The community reference count is increasing during the increment function. However, decrement functions are not called in one of the places after processing the routes update. This will lead to a disturbance of the continuity reference count, which will cause an rpd crash.

items.synopsis: Unexpected behavior of bandwidth based metric for IS-IS protocol
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms unexpected behavior of bandwidth based metric in IS-IS is seen since actual bandwidth is falling back to 0 bps when one of the member interface of AE (Aggregated Ethernet) bundle (interface-group) goes down.

items.synopsis: DHCP packets might not be sent to the clients when 'forward-only' is reconfigured under the routing instance
items.description: On all Junos platforms, reconfiguring 'forward-only' in any routing instance is leading to deactivate of [default:default] jdhcpd filter. Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) packets might not be sent to the clients.

items.synopsis: The DHCPv4 relay will send two option-82 to the server and the DHCP session will not be established
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCPv4) Relay is configured with forward-only mode along with "trust-option-82", DHCP-relay should not add another option 82 to the packet sent to the DHCP server. The DHCP server upon receiving the packet with two option-82 will respond only with 1st header of option-82 which might get dropped by the relay, thus the packet is not forwarded to the DHCP client and the DHCP session won't get established.

items.synopsis: Traffic loop is seen due to incorrect root bridge ID
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, in VSTP (Virtual Spanning-Tree Protocol) topology, whenever a new vlan is added in between previously configured vlan group followed by configuring the system-identifier, the bridge priority will change for existing vlans which might give incorrect system ID or bridge ID creating a traffic loop.

items.synopsis: mac-move-limit : MMAS flag not getting reset after interface recovers due to l2-learning restart
items.description: MMAS Flag will not be displayed for interface after it recovers due to l2-learning process restart

items.synopsis: MVPN tunnel is not synced to backup router
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, when OSPF inter-area is configured with segmented provider-tunnel and master undergoes MBB(make-before-break), the multicast route entry on backup router will not have the tunnel name synced with master.

items.synopsis: High CPU utilization is seen when chassisd is down during dynamic IFL creation
items.description: On all Junos platforms, in a very rare cases, while creating the specific dynamic IFls (PE-PIM (Protocol Independent Multicast) Encapsulation or PD-PIM Decapsulation), if the chassisd is down, the stuck entries in the Kernel Routing table (KRT) queue results in a high CPU utilization. The high CPU might hamper the rpd process functionality in rare cases and also device responsiveness will be slow.

items.synopsis: JDI-RCT : PPMD crashed at ppm_destroy_distrib_proto_stats_group_entry ( )
items.description: When l2cpd (in the context of xSTP) clears the entries that it has programmed on ppmd, ie when you delete xSTP configs from the box, there can be a possibility of ppmd core. If ppmd is in distributed mode then there will be no service impact, else there can be service impact as packet transmission for various protocols will happen via if ppmd is in centralized mode.

items.synopsis: Router Send RA with Router lifetime 0 when the upstream interface is shut
items.description: Issue: 1. This is a Day-1 issue with virtual RA. For virtual interfaces used in EVPN-VXLAN with multihoming scenario and VRRP, we will have two IPv6 link local addresses, one is the interface's link local address and another one is the virtual-gateway-address(VGA). There are two redundant gateways in this case which will have common VGA and in event of a failure of any given gateway, ND/RA re-resolution is not required. 2. Whenever interface is enabled or disabled, we get two link local IFA notifications for the same IFL. Only one link local IFA will be stored in the IPv6 interface at a time. 3. When second notification is received for the interface's link local address, it is treated as a link local address change and hence RA with 0 lifetime is sent for this IFA, but the source address is derived from virtual interface which is the VGA. 4. After receiving RA packet with lifetime zero, host VM deletes the default route to the VGA address and hence traffic loss is observed. 5. In this case, RA with 0 lifetime must not be sent as the VGA link local address is common and it is not changed by RPD clients (L2ALD for EVPN-VXLAN and VRRPD for VRRP). Fix: 1. As link local address will keep changing for virtual interface from virtual gateway address to configured link local address with every IFA notification, we don't need to send RA with lifetime 0 for virtual interface as the link local address for virtual interface can be changed only by RPD clients. Hence removed this part from the code for virtual interface only. 2. We need to send RA with lifetime 0 when RPD client sends an RA add request with different link local VGA. Hence added support to send RA with lifetime 0 if received VGA from RPD client is different from stored link local address in the virtual interface.

items.category: RPD Next-hop issues including indirect, CNH, and MCNH
items.synopsis: The rpd process might crash with back-to-back rpd restarts
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, the rpd process might crash if the rpd process restarts back-to-back before the rpd process comes up.

items.category: RPD route tables, resolver, routing instances, static routes
items.synopsis: Multipath route is not getting compute and skip the multipath eligibility check
items.description: On all Junos platforms, multipath route will not be formed correctly when a BGP route is received from RR (Route Reflector) and preference decided based on cluster list length.

items.synopsis: The FPC can go to a fault state on certain Junos Evolved PTX platforms after system reboot
items.description: On certain Junos Evolved PTX platforms FPC (Flexible PIC concentrator) goes to a fault state after a system reboots with a Major alarm - Power Failure. This issue is a rare issue and the FPC in a fault state will impact the data traffic. To recover from this issue the impacted FPCs need to be rebooted.

items.category: ZT/YTpfe bridging, learning, stp, oam, irb software
items.synopsis: VLAN tags are imposed incorrectly when traffic is routed over IRB going out of the access interface
items.description: On MX platforms, traffic egressing on the IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) interface with the underlying L2 (layer2) access port has VLAN tags imposed incorrectly.

items.synopsis: Commit failure might be observed on reactivation of jflow related configurations
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, reactivation of jflow (v9/ipfix) related configurations cannot be committed on backup RE.

items.description: On all Junos platforms, when the 'extend-size' knob is configured and a scaled configuration is committed, the rpd daemon crash is seen and the commit operation fails. root@device> show configuration | match configuration-database | display set set system configuration-database extend-size root@device# load update /var/tmp/New_config.txt load complete root@device# commit error: Check-out pass for Routing protocols process (/usr/sbin/rpd) dumped core (0x86) error: configuration check-out failed

items.synopsis: < ok/> response is getting generated along with < rpc-error>
items.description: When maximum-password-length is configured and the user tries to configure password whose length exceeds configured maximum-password-length, there is an error and the '' tag is emitted. (Ideally '' tag should not be emitted in an error scenario.) The configuration does not get committed.

items.description: On Junos Evolved QFX series platforms, all BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) flapped (due to many physical interfaces flapping) and evo application crashed (evo-pfemand) when Jvision IFL (Interface Logical) sensor is periodically streamed and the IFL is deleted.
